risk_reasons: The write site is the publisher's auto-approval downgrade, an approval-path decision that takes back a post already scheduled to reach Google.
The transaction it joins already holds the review, business and response anchors and completes an outbox attempt. A ledger failure aborts that whole downgrade.
It is the only lane with no tenant key in local scope, so it adds a tenant-key resolution inside a decision transaction.
goal: downgradeAutoApprovedResponseForManualReviewInTx records an auto_post_revoked Refusal against the response it takes back, using the account_id the transaction's existing business lock already reads.
non_goals: The three solicitation single lanes. #1010 owns them.
The outreach render lane. #1011 owns it.
The held_draft and policy_gate_held lanes. #1013 owns them, and #998 ruled these are three distinct acts rather than a double count.
The Restraint tab and any read over refusal_events. #1014 owns the read path.
The lane category map and the AutoPolicyDowngradeReason type move. The feat/refusal-lane-vocabulary prerequisite lands both on main before this branch arms.
Exporting resolveAccountIdFromBusiness from src/lib/approval/audit.ts. The owner chose to widen the existing business lock instead, so audit.ts is not edited.
Changing which responses are downgraded, when, or why. This slice records the decision and alters none of it.
user_visible_behavior: No owner-visible change. Nothing reads refusal_events until #1014.
A downgrade writes one refusal_events row against the response id, in the same transaction as the responses UPDATE, the approval audit row and the notification enqueue.
A no-op downgrade writes nothing, because no decision was made.
Setting REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false stops the write without a deploy and leaves downgrade behaviour byte-identical to today.
invariants: account_id comes from the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on businesses the transaction already issues. No second read, and no new error path: the existing missing-business guard already returns no-op.
occurredAt is the transaction-time sentinel. The decision and the write share one transaction and approval_audit_log.created_at is DEFAULT NOW(), so both rows agree to the microsecond.
subject_type is response and subject_id is the response id, never the audit row id. #1001 superseded #997 on this point.
refusal_code is the AutoPolicyDowngradeReason verbatim. judge_disabled and judge_unhealthy stay two codes even though they share one category and one audit marker.
The Refusal is written only after the guarded UPDATE returns a row. A no-op downgrade made no decision.
The ledger write is never caught at the call site. It aborts the downgrade, and the kill switch is the lever.
src/lib/refusals/write.ts is not edited. This lane consumes the single-row helper as shipped by #1009.
The standalone wrapper and every InTx caller reach exactly one write site, so neither arm can drift from the other.
Tenant isolation: every row carries account_id NOT NULL and the table keeps deny-all RLS.
edge_cases: The response is not downgradeable, the business is missing, or the review anchor is absent: the function returns no-op before the UPDATE and writes no Refusal.
The outbox attempt CAS fails: the function returns no-op and writes no Refusal.
The guarded UPDATE matches no row despite the earlier check: the function returns no-op and writes no Refusal.
The same response is downgraded twice: the partial unique index on (refusal_source, subject_id) leaves one row, and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING lets the second transaction commit.
All six AutoPolicyDowngradeReason members reach the write site: four through judge-gate.ts and two through auto-policy-publish.ts.
The standalone wrapper opens its own transaction while an InTx caller passes one already open: both reach the same single write site.
REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is false: the downgrade, its audit row and its notification enqueue are unchanged and the helper emits one warning per disabled episode.
A CHECK violation from a writer bug aborts the downgrade, so the response stays auto-approved and the outbox attempt is not completed. The publisher retries it.
existing_patterns_to_follow: src/lib/auto-approval/suspension.ts — the #1009 call-site precedent: writeRefusalEvent on the deciding transaction, after the guard that proves a decision was made, with no try/catch.
src/lib/refusals/write.ts — the single-row helper, its per-lane input union and the transaction-time sentinel.
worker/jobs/publisher/auto-policy-downgrade.ts — the existing lock ladder (reviews, businesses, responses) and the DOWNGRADE_MARKERS record the new map mirrors.
src/lib/approval/audit.ts insertAuditLogAutoPolicy — the write the Refusal sits beside, and the reason approval_audit_log.created_at and occurred_at agree.
src/lib/refusals/vocabulary.ts — the auto_post_revoked map landed by the feat/refusal-lane-vocabulary prerequisite.
test_seams: worker/jobs/publisher/judge-gate.ts — the four callers that choose a judge-related reason.
worker/jobs/publisher/auto-policy-publish.ts — the two callers that choose an entitlement or suspension reason.
tests_to_add: a downgrade writes exactly one refusal_events row against the response id
a downgrade's refusal_events row carries subject_type response, never the approval audit row id
a downgrade's refusal_events row carries the account_id read by the transaction's existing business lock
a downgrade's refusal_events row carries occurred_at equal to the approval_audit_log created_at written by the same transaction
a downgrade records the AutoPolicyDowngradeReason verbatim, so judge_disabled and judge_unhealthy stay two codes
every AutoPolicyDowngradeReason maps to a Refusal category and the downgrade writes it
a no-op downgrade on a response that is not downgradeable writes no refusal_events row
a no-op downgrade on a missing business writes no refusal_events row
a downgrade that loses the outbox attempt CAS writes no refusal_events row
downgrading the same response twice leaves one refusal_events row and lets the second transaction commit
the standalone wrapper and the in-transaction caller each write exactly one refusal_events row
a ledger failure rolls back the downgrade, the approval audit row and the notification enqueue together

rollback_plan: Three layers. (1) REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false on Railway stops the ledger write with no deploy and leaves the downgrade byte-identical to today; invoke the flag-flip skill. (2) Revert the PR on main and redeploy, which removes the call site and the widened business lock together. (3) No down migration: migration 116 stays and rows already written are not deleted. ArchivalPoller's refusal_events arm landed in #1009 and is untouched, so surviving rows still age out at REFUSAL_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS.
observability: One warning per disabled episode from the helper whenever REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED is false.
A ledger failure here reaches Sentry through attachJobFailureSink on the terminal BullMQ attempt, because both caller lanes run inside ResponsePublisherWorker.

Reconciliation query for staging: COUNT(*) of refusal_events WHERE refusal_source = 'auto_post_revoked' must equal the count of approval_audit_log rows carrying an auto-policy revoked action, per account, inside the retention window.
